finding: §3.1 states the delete-before-spawn rule as "the driver then deletes the file of every unit that set does contain, immediately before spawning it", and test 45 (§10.6) repeats it as "the driver deletes the file of every unit the oracle did return before spawning it". Read literally that covers all eight kinds of §3.3, so the driver would delete a `review-record`/`audit-record` unit's durable write — `$TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson` and the recorded round file — before re-spawning it, destroying cycle state. That contradicts test 17 (§10.2), which scopes the deletion to "its role findings file", and contradicts §3.4's invariant that no driver action ever unrecords a round and §3.1's own rule that the driver mutates no cycle state (it never holds the task-file write lock; writes belong to the children).
suggestion: Scope the rule explicitly to role units in both places: "the driver deletes the findings file of every `review-role`/`audit-role` unit that set contains, immediately before spawning it; no other kind's durable write is ever removed by the driver", and reword test 45 to match test 17.

finding: `runner` takes "a built-in template name, a runner object, or a map from unit kind to either of those with a `default` key", but a runner object and a per-kind map are both JSON objects and the spec names no discriminator. `{"cmd":"claude","args":[...]}` and `{"implement":"claude","default":{...}}` are decoded by the same `json.Unmarshal` call; the implementer must invent the rule (presence of `cmd`? presence of `default`? all-values-are-objects-or-strings?). The stated error case "a map missing `default` is a usage error" is also unreachable without that rule — a map missing `default` is indistinguishable from a runner object missing `cmd`, so the two produce different messages depending on a guess.
suggestion: State the discriminator explicitly, e.g. "an object carrying a `cmd` key is a runner object; any other object is a per-kind map, whose keys must all be unit kinds from §3.3 plus `default`", and say which error each malformed shape produces.

finding: The `review-resolve` durable write is "Every finding in the round's file carries a disposition", but "the round's file" is never resolved to a path. The same round has two candidate files — `$TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson` (what `review-record` wrote) and the recorded round file under `.tp-review/` — and this round pinned the file for `audit-fix` ("the results file is the one the round's `audit-record` unit wrote, `$TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson`") while leaving the review mirror unpinned. Test 18 ("each predicate is decidable from one file") cannot be written for `review-resolve` without picking one, and two engineers will pick differently.
suggestion: State the review-side path explicitly in the same sentence shape used for `audit-fix`: the round's findings file is `$TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson`, the file `review-record` wrote and `tp review --resolve` updates in place. Also say whether *every* finding must carry a disposition or only blocking ones, since a low-severity row left undisposed decides the predicate.

finding: §6.3's central claim — the reviewer and auditor "may write exactly one path ... and are denied every other write" — has no test anywhere in §10. Test 24 asserts only plugin validation and hook fixtures, test 27 the emitted path, test 44 the `--agent` mapping. The claim is also not obviously observable as written: the escalation record is written by the `tp escalate` process through a shell, and §6.2 puts shell tools outside the write matcher, so an allowlist over Write/Edit tools can neither grant nor deny it. A QA engineer cannot tell what artifact to assert against.
suggestion: Add a test to §10.4 that pins the observable: e.g. the shipped `agents/tp-reviewer.json` declares an allow entry for `$TP_ROUND_DIR/role-*.ndjson` and no other write path, asserted against the file. Separately state that the escalation record is out of scope of the tool allowlist because it is written by the `tp` process, so no test is expected to cover it there.

finding: Test 27 was not realigned with the two properties round 11 introduced in §6.3. It still says tp review/tp audit "emit the round-scoped findings path" (singular) although the emitted path is now per role — each role's prompt naming role-<that role's id>.ndjson — and it says the record unit "merges that directory" although the point of the role- prefix is that merged.ndjson sits deliberately outside the role-*.ndjson input glob. Nothing in §10 asserts that a merge never re-ingests its own output, which is the exact defect the rename was written to prevent.
suggestion: Extend test 27: assert each role's emitted filename carries that role's id, and assert that a record unit run twice in one round merges only the role files and does not read back merged.ndjson.

finding: §10.7 claims "no other command's exit codes change outside `TP_UNATTENDED=1`", but §8a.4 changes `tp review --merge` and `tp audit --merge` from always exiting 0 to exiting 1 when an input has content lines and none parsed — an exit-code change on an existing command, outside unattended mode, asserted by tests 32 and 49. The inventory of invalidated tests therefore under-reports what the change breaks, which is exactly the section a migration task reads.
suggestion: Add the merge change to §10.7: name `tp review --merge` / `tp audit --merge` as gaining a non-zero exit for a wholly-unparseable input, and state that any existing test asserting exit 0 over a malformed-input fixture moves in the same task as §8a.4; then narrow the blanket sentence accordingly.

finding: "The driver then deletes the file of every unit that set does contain, immediately before spawning it" — and test 45 repeats it as "deletes the file of every unit the oracle did return". Only role units have a defined file. For `implement`, `decompose`, the two record kinds and `audit-fix`, "the file" is undefined, and a literal reading would have the driver delete a re-attempted `review-record` unit's `merged.ndjson` before respawning it. Test 45 and test 17 will be written to contradictory scopes.
suggestion: Scope the sentence to role units: "the driver deletes the findings file of every *role* unit the returned set contains, immediately before spawning it", and state explicitly that no other kind's artifact is removed before an attempt. Restate test 45 in the same terms.

finding: §3.1's pre-spawn deletion rule — "the driver then deletes the file of every unit that set does contain, immediately before spawning it", echoed verbatim in test 45 — was written when only role units had a named file. Round 11 gave review-record and audit-record a file-named predicate ($TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson), so the rule now literally sweeps merged.ndjson before a record unit is spawned. That collides with §3.3's audit-fix, which disposes its row inside that same merged.ndjson: a re-attempted audit-record regenerates the file from role-*.ndjson and drops every disposition already written into it. Test 17 still describes the deletion as "its role findings file", so the two tests disagree about the rule's scope.
suggestion: Scope the deletion rule explicitly to role units (the only kind whose leftover can falsely satisfy a retry's predicate) and say that a record unit's merged.ndjson is overwritten in place, never pre-deleted; realign test 45's wording with test 17's.

finding: `TP_RUNNER_SEAM` "outranks every layer of §7's precedence, including a CLI flag" and is inherited by children through the parent-environment merge, while §5.1 fences `runner` so "under the variable a unit cannot set them at all, at any layer". Test 40 ("`runner` and `notify_cmd` cannot be set at any layer") must run inside a harness that sets `TP_RUNNER_SEAM`, so the test's own precondition is a live override of the field it asserts is unsettable. The spec never says whether the seam is stripped from the child environment, whether the fence outranks the seam, or whether the seam is simply out of the fence's scope.
suggestion: Pin one rule: either the driver strips `TP_RUNNER_SEAM` from every child's environment (like the `TP_UNATTENDED` merge rule), or state that the seam is a driver-process-only input never consulted by a child, so the fence and the seam cannot collide. Say which, and have test 40 assert it.

finding: `decompose`'s durable write is "The task file holds at least one task", which is satisfiable by work that is not done: a unit that imports 3 of the 13 tasks the spec needs, or that imports one placeholder, exits 0 with the predicate met and the driver advances to the implement phase with an incomplete task set. Every other kind's predicate is scoped to the unit's own subject (this role's file, this task's status, this row's disposition); `decompose`'s is a property of the file as a whole and cannot distinguish a complete decomposition from a partial one. It is also the one predicate that can be true before the unit runs — a re-entered decompose phase over a non-empty task file passes without the child doing anything.
suggestion: Either scope the predicate to the run ("the task file gained at least one task since the unit was spawned" — accepting that it becomes a delta, contrary to the surrounding paragraph), or state explicitly that completeness of the decomposition is the oracle's business via `tp validate` coverage and that this predicate only proves the import happened.

finding: `review-resolve`'s durable write is "Every finding in the round's file carries a disposition", but "the round's file" is never resolved for the review side the way §3.3's following paragraph resolves it for `audit-fix` (`$TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson`). There are two candidates with different contents — `$TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson`, which the `review-record` unit wrote, and the recorded round file under `.tp-review/`, which is what `tp review --resolve` operates on today — and the driver has to open one of them to evaluate the predicate. Separately, "every finding" makes the unit fail while any non-blocking finding is undisposed, which may or may not be the intent given convergence counts blocking findings.
suggestion: Name the exact path the `review-resolve` predicate is evaluated over, and state whether "every finding" means every row in that file or only the rows that count against convergence.

finding: "A unit is attempted `1 + run_max_unit_retries` times" has no place in §3.1's loop, which is six steps with no retry branch (read state, releasable?, take `next_units`, spawn, re-read state, check caps). A retry is therefore either an inner loop inside step 4 or a fresh iteration — and the two differ observably: caps are "evaluated between iterations only", so an inner-loop retry cannot trip `cap-wall-clock`, while a fresh-iteration retry re-polls the oracle, which may not return the same unit. The concurrent case compounds it: when two of five role units fail, the spec does not say whether the driver retries just those two, re-spawns the whole set, or waits for the next iteration.
suggestion: Add the retry to §3.1's loop as an explicit step, state whether attempts of the same `(kind, id)` re-consult the oracle, and say whether caps are evaluated between attempts.

finding: "A unit is attempted `1 + run_max_unit_retries` times", but §3.1's six-step loop has no retry step, so it is undecidable whether a retry happens inside the same iteration or as a fresh iteration. The choice is observable and changes three tests: with in-iteration retries, "caps are evaluated between iterations only" lets a unit burn every attempt past `run_max_units` (test 3, test 33), and test 21's "stops the run only once the unit's attempts are exhausted" implies immediate retry; with per-iteration retries the oracle is re-consulted and must return the same unit again.
suggestion: Add the retry to §3.1's loop explicitly — e.g. a step 4b: a failed unit is respawned immediately, up to its attempt budget, before step 5 — and state whether the cap check in step 6 can be reached mid-retry. Then test 8 and test 33 have one reading.

finding: §3.4 documents overshoot for two of three caps — "a run can overshoot its wall-clock and budget caps by at most one iteration" — but `cap-units` counts "spawned children", and an iteration can spawn N concurrent role units at once. With `run_max_units` at 99 and five active roles the driver either spawns all five (overshooting to 104) or spawns none. Neither is stated, and unlike wall-clock the counter is knowable *before* spawning, so "between iterations only" is a choice rather than a necessity.
suggestion: State whether `run_max_units` is checked per iteration (and may overshoot by the concurrency width) or per spawn, and if per iteration, add units to the overshoot sentence so all three caps read alike.

finding: §3.4 says "Caps are evaluated between iterations only" and then bounds the consequence to two caps: "a run can overshoot its wall-clock and budget caps by at most one iteration". The same mechanism overshoots `run_max_units`: one iteration spawns every role unit of the phase concurrently (§3.3), and `cap-units` counts spawned children including retries, so a run whose count is one below the cap still spawns N role children before the next check. The stated overshoot set contradicts the stated evaluation point.
suggestion: Either include `cap-units` in the overshoot sentence ("its unit, wall-clock and budget caps by at most one iteration, where an iteration may spawn one child per active role"), or state that the driver refuses to start an iteration whose concurrent unit set would exceed `run_max_units` and stops with `cap-units` instead.

finding: Round 11 added "phase" to the run-state schema, but the same paragraph still declares run state "observability, not truth" and calls two sources of truth for one fact "the drift the overnight postmortem catalogued" — phase is already owned by the cycle state the oracle reports. Nothing says when the key is written or updated, yet §10.1 test 2 has a single run advance through implement, review and audit, so a run traverses several phases while the file holds one value; and §3.5's own audit-phase branch for --status (spec_coverage_clean_rounds, role_streaks, divergence) now has two candidate sources, one of which is stale for a crashed run. No test in §10 covers the new key.
suggestion: Either state that "phase" is rewritten on every iteration and that --status still derives the audit-phase branch from the cycle state (never from run state), or drop the key and have --status read phase from the oracle. Whichever is chosen, add a test asserting the phase --status reports after a mid-run phase change.

finding: The log path is `$TP_RUN_DIR/<seq>-<kind>-<id>.jsonl`, and §3.1 makes an `audit-fix` unit's `id` the finding's `role:item_id`. `item_id` is auditor-authored text, so an id can contain `:`, `/`, spaces or a leading `.`, and no sanitization or escaping rule is given. Test 17 ("a retried unit gets a fresh log path") and test 37 cannot be written deterministically for `audit-fix`, and an `item_id` containing a slash yields an unwritable path.
suggestion: Pin the filename derivation — e.g. every non-`[A-Za-z0-9._-]` character in `<id>` is replaced with `-` before it enters a filename — and add a test that an `audit-fix` unit whose `item_id` contains `/` and `:` gets a writable, unique log path.

finding: `next_units` "omits any role whose findings file already satisfies §3.3's predicate", but §3.1 defines `TP_ROUND_DIR` as an environment variable the driver sets for *children*, and the spec never says how `tp resume` — invoked as the oracle — locates the round directory. A test for test 45 or test 52 must decide whether to export `TP_ROUND_DIR` before running `tp resume --json` or to rely on the command deriving `.tp/rounds/<base>/<phase>-r<round>` itself, and the two setups give different results outside a run.
suggestion: State that `tp resume` derives the round directory from base, phase and round on its own and never reads `TP_ROUND_DIR` (or the converse), so the oracle, the driver and the Stop hook of test 52 have one documented way to find the file.

finding: §4.1 makes `next_action`'s `command`, `brief_command` and `payload` render `next_units[0]` whenever the array is non-empty, but §8a.2 requires `next_action`'s mechanize branch (precedence step 3) to carry a class name and the phase qualifier — a branch that today exists precisely during the review phase, when `next_units` is non-empty with role units. The two rules collide over the same object and the spec never says which fields the mechanize branch may still own (presumably `summary` only), so the §8a.2 task and the §4.1 task can each be implemented as written and produce contradictory output.
suggestion: State in §4.1 which `next_action` fields `next_units[0]` overwrites and which the existing branches keep (e.g. `summary` and any branch-specific keys are unaffected), and have §8a.2 name the field the qualifier lands in.

finding: `last_failure` has two implied writers with no owner named. "a unit exits non-zero" is observable only by the driver, while "closes with a failed quality gate" with "the gate's own output" is observable only inside the child's own `tp done`; a gate failure need not make the harness exit non-zero (§5.2 establishes that the harness's exit code need not carry the inner command's). Two writers on one unlocked file is the same two-sources-of-truth pattern §3.5 rejects for run state, and it interacts badly with §5.2's rule that an escalating unit "sets no `last_failure`" — the driver can suppress its own write, but not one a child already made.
suggestion: Name the single owner: either the driver writes `last_failure` in all cases (and the gate summary reaches it from the child's exit path via a tp-authored artifact), or `tp` itself writes it whenever a tp command fails inside a unit and the driver only writes it for a non-zero exit with no existing record for that `(unit_kind, unit_id)`. State the write discipline (atomic replace) and how §5.2's suppression applies to a record a child already wrote.

finding: `last_failure` has two writers on two different sides of the process boundary — the driver ("when a unit exits non-zero") and the child ("or closes with a failed quality gate", which only `tp done` can observe) — and the spec never says which writes what, nor what happens when a `tp done` gate fails outside a run. `unit_kind` and `unit_id` come from the child's environment, so a gate failure in an ordinary interactive session has no values for them, yet `tp resume` and `tp brief` "surface `last_failure` when one is present" unconditionally. The implementer must guess whether to skip the write outside a run, write with empty ids, or invent a sentinel — and the clear rule keys on `(unit_kind, unit_id)`, so a record with empty ids can never be cleared.
suggestion: Split the two writers explicitly: state that the driver writes on a non-zero child exit, that `tp done` writes on a failed gate only when the unit env vars are present, and what (if anything) is recorded for a gate failure outside a run.

finding: §5.1 fences `runner` and `notify_cmd` "at any layer" and test 40 asserts they "cannot be set at any layer", but §7 says `notify_cmd` is per-operator and "read from `.tp/local.json` only" — it has no CLI, env, task-override or project-config layer to refuse, and §6.2 already denies writes to `.tp/local.json`. The fence for `notify_cmd` therefore names refusals at layers the resolution rule says do not exist, and §5.1's env-layer rule (`TP_` + upper-cased field name) implies a `TP_NOTIFY_CMD` layer that §7 contradicts.
suggestion: Reconcile the two: either §7 gives `notify_cmd` the normal layered path (so the fence has something to refuse), or §5.1 says explicitly that `notify_cmd` has no settable layer and the fence is the §6.2 write denial plus a refusal of any `tp set`/`tp config` route that would create one — and test 40 asserts that shape instead.

finding: `tp escalate` must write `{decision, unit_kind, unit_id, phase, evidence, options[], at}`, and it runs inside the child. §3.1 enumerates the child's environment — `TP_RUN_ID`, `TP_UNIT_ID`, `TP_UNIT_KIND`, `TP_UNIT_SEQ`, `TP_ROUND`, `TP_RUN_DIR`, `TP_ROUND_DIR`, `TP_FILE` — and there is no `TP_PHASE`. Every other field has an env source; `phase` has none, so the implementer must either add a variable the spec does not document or make `tp escalate` re-run the oracle (a second discovery + state read, whose answer can differ from the phase the driver spawned the unit in).
suggestion: Either add `TP_PHASE` to §3.1's variable list, or state in §5.2 that `tp escalate` derives `phase` from the cycle state at write time and accept that it is the phase at escalation, not at spawn.

finding: The three hooks are given behaviour but no implementation vehicle, and one of them is not trivially scriptable: the Stop hook must apply §3.3's predicate, i.e. confirm that *every line* of `$TP_ROUND_DIR/role-$TP_UNIT_ID.ndjson` parses as JSON. §6.1 states the Go binary is deliberately not shipped inside the plugin, so the hook cannot be a tp subcommand unless it shells out to a `tp` that §6.1 only guarantees is on `PATH` after the SessionStart preflight has run. Whether the hooks are shell scripts, a hidden tp subcommand (`tp hook stop`), or something else decides whether NDJSON validation, `stop_hook_active` handling and the 10-second timeout (§6.4) are cheap or awkward, and the implementer currently picks.
suggestion: Name the vehicle: state whether the shipped hooks are POSIX shell scripts that invoke a tp subcommand (and which one), and if they call `tp`, say what the hook does when the preflight has not passed.

finding: The repair meant to carve the escalation record out of the reviewer/auditor write allowlist, but the sentence now reads "may write exactly one path — their own findings file at $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-$TP_UNIT_ID.ndjson, plus the escalation record tp escalate writes on their behalf": "exactly one path" and "plus" a second path contradict each other in one clause. It is also the wrong fence — §5.2 has tp escalate write the record, and §6.2 puts shell tools outside the matcher, so a Write-tool allowlist never governs that file.
suggestion: Keep the allowlist at exactly one path (the role findings file) and move the escalation record out of it entirely, noting that it reaches disk through tp escalate, which the tool restrictions do not mediate.

finding: Test 12 asserts "A run.json row exists with null `exit_code`", but the run state file is named `.tp/run-<base>.json` everywhere else (§3.5, test 15). "run.json" is not a file this spec defines, so the assertion names a path that does not exist.
suggestion: Rewrite test 12 as "a `.tp/run-<base>.json` unit row exists with null `exit_code`, `duration_seconds` and `spend_usd` before its child exits and is updated in place after".

finding: Test 19 covers only one half of §5.1's narrowed budget-0 fence: "setting a budget field to 0 while a non-zero value resolves exits 2". The other half §5.1 states explicitly — setting 0 where 0 already resolves changes nothing and is accepted — has no assertion, and it is the half a naive implementation (refuse any 0) gets wrong.
suggestion: Add to test 19: with the resolved value already 0, setting the same budget field to 0 under TP_UNATTENDED=1 exits 0.

finding: §3.2.1 defines the `claude` template's `args` as a closed list with exactly one documented conditional addition (the `--max-budget-usd` pair). §6.3 then adds a second, undocumented-there conditional append — `["--agent", "<name>"]` per unit kind — so the canonical definition of the template no longer describes what the driver actually spawns, and a reader implementing §3.2.1 alone produces a runner that never selects an agent.
suggestion: State the full composition in §3.2.1 — base args, then the budget pair when `run_max_unit_budget_usd` is non-zero, then the `--agent` pair for the kinds §6.3 names — and leave §6.3 owning only which agent maps to which kind.

finding: The driver "reads one number from the final line of that unit's log" via `total_cost_usd` or the declared `spend_key`, but nothing says what happens when a runner that *declares* a key produces a final line that is not JSON, is empty (a crashed child, a truncated stream), or lacks the key. The `spend: null` path is documented only for runners declaring no key at all, so the implementer must decide between recording null, failing the unit, and treating it as 0 — and the choice changes whether `cap-budget` can be evaded by a runner that dies mid-write.
suggestion: State that an unreadable or key-less final line records `spend: null` for that unit, does not fail the unit, and is reported once, so budget accrual degrades visibly rather than silently.

finding: The audit-fix paragraph rewritten in round 11 ends "the kind has no way to record the no-code-change outcome §3.3 admits" — a pointer to the section the sentence is already inside, left over from when the justification sat elsewhere. A reader following it lands back where they started.
suggestion: Replace "§3.3 admits" with "the table above admits" (or "this section's table").

finding: `notify_cmd` is "exec'd without a shell, split on whitespace" (§5.2) and typed as "Any command string" (§7), which makes any argument containing a space unexpressible — a script under a path with a space, or a message argument. There is no quoting rule and no array form, so an operator on macOS whose script lives under a spaced directory has no working configuration and no error telling them why.
suggestion: Either accept an array form for `notify_cmd` alongside the string, or state the quoting rule the splitter honours and what a malformed value does.

finding: §7's `runner` row gives Range as "Built-in name or object", omitting the third shape §3.2 defines — a map from unit kind to a name or object with a required `default` key, whose absence is a usage error. §7 is the table a `tp config --resolved` / `tp validate --project` task validates against, so the validator derived from it would reject the per-kind map that §3.2 and §3.2.2 both depend on. Test 16's "accepts both range endpoints, and rejects one step outside each" also has no meaning for `runner` and `notify_cmd`, which have no numeric endpoints.
suggestion: Extend the `runner` Range cell to "built-in name, runner object, or per-kind map with a required `default`", give `notify_cmd` its validation rule, and reword test 16 so the endpoint assertion applies to the five numeric fields only, with a separate shape assertion for `runner`/`notify_cmd`.
